previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and migraines, was admitted for adrenal crisis triggered by gastroenteritis and a missed prednisone dose. She presented with hypotension, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and was treated with IV fluids and stress-dose steroids, which stabilized her blood pressure. Lab results revealed acute kidney injury and anion gap metabolic acidosis due to dehydration, both of which resolved with rehydration. Markedly elevated liver enzymes were attributed to unintentional acetaminophen overdose; she was treated with IV acetylcysteine for two days with improvement. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli was identified and treated with antibiotics, transitioning to oral cefpodoxime at discharge. An EGD ruled out esophagitis. She was discharged on a prednisone taper, antibiotics, and instructions to avoid acetaminophen, with follow-up arranged.
